needs_reteach.flow: Trigger dedicated visual re-teach. Ezy models another cartoon concept. Provide a physical playground before testing again.

careless_slip.flow: Inject a quick morning visual warm-up directly into the dashboard. Do not block next lesson.

mastered.flow: Inject spaced diagnostic checks to ensure long-term retention.

fables.title: Fables Diagnostic Workbook (Page 6 & 12)
fables.task: Differentiate animal character traits based on text evidence.

interactive_questions.question: Which word from the text shows that Hyena worked hard for Cockerel?

clue_board.clue_1: Look at Page 6, line 4: 'when he did his chores for him.'
clue_board.clue_2: Chores are daily household jobs. If Hyena plowed the fields and did Cockerel's chores, he was working very hard!

interactive_questions.question: What is Cockerel's true personality trait when he lets Hyena do all the hard work?

clue_board.clue_1: Cockerel sat in the shade and watched, with his feet up on an old table under the trees.
clue_board.clue_2: Someone who rests while others work under the hot sun is acting lazy!

grammar.title: Complex Connective Trailing (Page 15)
grammar.task: Differentiate Compound vs. Complex Sentences using because, after, unless, although, until.

interactive_questions.question: Complete this sentence: '___ the sky broke apart, the colours flooded through.'

clue_board.clue_1: Look at Page 16, line 5: 'When the sky broke apart...'
clue_board.clue_2: This is a Complex sentence because it starts with a dependent clause using the time connective 'When'!

biography.title: Poorna Malavath Timeline Matcher (Page 26)
biography.task: Map events onto a chronological mountaineering ladder.

interactive_questions.question: Poorna was born on 10 June 2000. When did she train in Darjeeling for eight months?

clue_board.clue_1: Look at Paragraph 3 on Page 26: 'In 2013, Malavath was sent to train in Darjeeling...'
clue_board.clue_2: Her training came after school selection, but before her historic Everest climb in May 2014.

easy.title: Unit 1: Fables Comprehension (Tiered: Easy)
easy.instructions: Simple reading & vocabulary with Ezy's interactive hints enabled.

questions.question: In 'Why Cockerels Crow', why was Cockerel admired by everyone?
options: He ploughed the fields for Hyena.
He had a bright red spiky comb on his head.
He could fly higher than the magpies.
questions.answer: He had a bright red spiky comb on his head.
questions.hint: Look at the very first line of page 6! What did Cockerel wear on top of his head like flames?

moderate.title: Unit 1: Fables Analysis (Tiered: Moderate)
moderate.instructions: Analyzing implicit meanings and sentence types. No direct hints during execution.

questions.question: Why did Hyena's wife ask her husband: 'What about our own family?'
options: She wanted him to buy a new house.
She felt he was exhausted from doing chores only for Cockerel.
She wanted him to cook food for her.
She was angry at Cockerel's spiky comb.
questions.answer: She felt he was exhausted from doing chores only for Cockerel.
questions.model_answer_rubric: Grounded in page 6. Score correct if student mentions Hyena's exhaustion, doing chores for Cockerel while leaving his own family work neglected.

tough.title: Unit 1: Fables Evaluation (Tiered: Tough)
tough.instructions: Synthesizing themes and writing/verbal explanations. Scored with verbal Reasoning log.

questions.question: Explain how Hyena's opinion of Cockerel changes from the beginning to the end of the fable. Use text evidence.

rubric.criteria: Student must trace the transition from friendship/respect to feeling deceived.

points.beginning: Hyena was respectul, did all his chores, and thought Cockerel was sacred/dangerous [Page 6]
points.climax: Hyena realized Cockerel's spiky comb couldn't make fire and that Cockerel lied [Page 9]
points.ending: Hyena realized he was tricked and Cockerel escaped into the trees [Page 9]
